title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche, continuation, around p. 700–706). Π_0 is the (discrete or profinite) fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, which is free on two generators. M = Π_0^ab ≅ Z^3/Z(1,1,1) is generated by the loop classes λ_0, λ_1, λ_∞ with λ_0+λ_1+λ_∞ = 0. S_3 permutes the three punctures and acts on M through this permutation module modulo the diagonal, which is the 2‑dimensional (root/weight lattice A_2 type) representation. In particular M^{S_3} = 0, and 1+ρ+ρ^2 = 0 on M for ρ of order 3.

H^+ is a central extension of S_3 by μ = {1,ω}. Its generators satisfy ρ^3 = σ^2 = ω and σρσ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}, so H^+ is the binary dihedral group of order 12 (Dic_3). The group 𝔖^+ = 𝔖_0/[Π_0,Π_0] is an extension of H^+ ≅ 𝔖_0/Π_0 by M. Everything is also done as sheaves of groups over an arbitrary base S, and over Spec Ẑ with a Ẑ^*-twist.

The page studies splittings of 𝔖^+ → H^+.
- Any lift of the generators has the form ρ' = ξρ, σ' = ησ with ξ, η sections of M (267).
- A splitting must send the central element ω to a central element of 𝔖^+. Since M ∩ Cent(𝔖^+) = M^{S_3} = 0, the centre maps injectively to {1,ω} (268), so ω must go to ω itself.
- So the conditions are ρ'^3 = σ'^2 = ω and σ'ρ'σ'^{-1} = ρ'^{-1}.
- Expanding gives (ξρ)^3 = ξ·ρ(ξ)·ρ^2(ξ)·ω and (ησ)^2 = η·σ(η)·ω. The first two conditions become the norm equations (1+ρ_M+ρ_M^2)ξ = 0 and (1+σ_M)η = 0, which are the earlier equations (245), (246).
- The first holds automatically, so ξ is arbitrary. The second forces η into the anti-invariant line: η = bδ = b(λ_1 − λ_0) (247).
- The braid-type relation σ'(ρ') = ρ'^{-1} is handled as on p. 700' and leads to (249)/(250) on the next page.

Outcome (next page): splittings exist and form a torsor under K ≅ Z^2. K is identified with M acting by conjugation, so any two splittings are conjugate by a unique section of M. Passing to the quotient by the centre μ gives a bijection with the splittings of 𝔖^+/μ over S_3. Cohomologically this is H^1(H^+, M) = 0 = H^0(H^+, M), plus vanishing of the extension class, checked explicitly.

The purpose is to normalise lifts of the S_3 symmetry of P^1 − {0,1,∞} at the abelianised level of π_1. This is the first step of the GT-style analysis of lifts of the order‑2 and order‑3 automorphisms, compatibly with the Galois / Ẑ^* action.
errors: No genuine error. One implicit step: the argument that ω must go to ω uses that the chosen lift ω ∈ 𝔖^+ is itself central (it acts trivially on M and is central modulo M). This is presumably established earlier and is consistent with (268).
The equality M^{S_3} = (something) in (268) is partly struck out and illegible. Mathematically it should be 0 (trivial), since the S_3-module Z^3/Z has no invariants.

ideas.what: Parametrising lifts of generators of a group extension by M-sections and reducing the relations to norm equations (1+ρ+ρ^2)ξ = 0, (1+σ)η = 0
ideas.modern_name: nonabelian 1-cocycle / splitting computation for extensions with abelian kernel

ideas.what: Splittings of 𝔖^+ = 𝔖_0/[Π_0,Π_0] over the binary S_3 (order 12) form an M-torsor, all conjugate under M, and correspond bijectively to splittings over S_3 after dividing by the centre
ideas.modern_name: H^1(Dic_3, Z^3/Z) = 0 and H^0 = 0; abelianised (metabelian level-1) normalisation of S_3-lifts on π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞})
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in Ihara, Drinfeld (GT), Lochak–Schneps-type normalisations of θ, ω-lifts
ideas.where_published: Not published; the Longue Marche manuscripts discuss related S_3/Teichmüller tower material

ideas.what: Using the centre (M^{S_3} = 0) to force a splitting to send ω to ω

deep.surprise_reason: Routine cohomological computation of splittings at the abelianised level. It is part of Grothendieck's detailed working-out of S_3 symmetry for P^1 minus three points, interesting archivally but containing nothing beyond standard results.
transcription_corrections: 'elles sont ξ arithmétiques' should read 'ξ arbitraire' (ξ arbitrary), since (1+ρ+ρ^2) = 0 on M.
'elles sont η revient' should read roughly 'pour η revient à (247) η = bδ = b(λ_1−λ_0)'; the trailing 'λ∈Γ' is more likely 'b ∈ Γ(S, ...)' (a section of the coefficient sheaf).
In (268), M ∩ Cent(𝔖^+) = M^{S_3} is followed by a struck-out symbol. The intended value is trivial (0/1), and Cent(𝔖^+) ≃ μ_𝔖 = {1,ω}_𝔖.
